name: How do I avoid losing all my storage when I open up the kitchen?

mainEntity.name: How do I avoid losing all my storage when I open up the kitchen?

acceptedAnswer.text: An open plan can preserve storage if storage is designed as part of the new room rather than left to the old walls. Tall cabinetry, a pantry, island drawers, appliance garages, built-ins, bench storage, and concealed utility zones can replace some lost wall capacity. Context: Removing a wall may eliminate upper cabinets, broom storage, outlets, or a place for small appliances, even when the room feels larger. Key factors: inventory; appliance storage; cleaning supplies; pantry needs; visual clutter. Practical guidance: List everything currently stored near the wall and assign each item a new location before approving the opening. Show door swings and drawer clearances on the plan. Elite Remodeling & Design’s kitchen remodeling scope includes layout, storage, cabinetry, and countertop planning.
acceptedAnswer.description: Inventory what the existing wall and nearby cabinets store, then replace that capacity with a pantry, tall cabinets, island drawers, built-ins, appliance storage, or concealed utility zones. Show every cabinet opening and appliance location on the plan so the larger room does not become harder to keep organized.
